record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.original_question: How can pre-equilibrium photon and dilepton production in heavy-ion collisions be calculated accurately and consistently across the free-streaming regime, the hydrodynamization transition, and the hydrodynamic regime, while moving beyond simplified conformal boost-invariant 0+1-dimensional systems that neglect transverse inhomogeneities?

evidence.quote: If we think of the applicability of hydrodynamics in terms of the relaxation time of the medium’s constituents τ_relax and the evolution time of the medium τ_evolution, we can broadly categorize the early stage of the collisions in the three regimes shown in Table 1
Photons and dileptons can be produced in all stages, and a consistent description of these different stages is necessary to calculate accurately electromagnetic emission in heavy-ion collisions.

One approach to study pre-equilibrium photons and dileptons is to focus on conformal boost-invariant systems where inhomogeneities in the plane transverse are neglected; this leads to simplified 0 + 1D systems where photon and dilepton production can be calculated in great detail using kinetic theory and holography.
In general, computing pre-equilibrium photons and dileptons in heavy-ion collisions require additional modeling beyond conformal 0 + 1D systems

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a high-energy heavy-ion collision modeled as a relativistic many-body system whose evolution passes through three successive regimes characterized by the ratio of the microscopic relaxation time τ_relax to the macroscopic evolution time τ_evolution: (i) a far-from-equilibrium free-streaming regime in which τ_relax ≫ τ_evolution and partonic constituents propagate quasi-freely; (ii) a hydrodynamization transition regime in which τ_relax ~ τ_evolution and the system rapidly approaches an effective fluid description; and (iii) a hydrodynamic regime in which τ_relax ≪ τ_evolution and viscous relativistic hydrodynamics applies. In each regime, electromagnetic radiation (real photons and dileptons, i.e. virtual photons decaying to lepton pairs) is produced from the strongly interacting medium with a rate determined by the electromagnetic current–current correlator evaluated in the appropriate underlying microscopic theory (e.g. QCD kinetic theory at weak coupling or holographic strongly-coupled gauge theory).

Existing detailed computations of pre-equilibrium photon and dilepton production assume a conformal, boost-invariant, transversely homogeneous 0+1-dimensional background, in which all fields depend only on proper time and the system has exact longitudinal boost invariance and no transverse spatial dependence.

Develop a framework that:
(a) defines and computes the differential photon and dilepton production rates dN/(d^4x d^3k) (or d^4k) consistently as functions of spacetime and momentum across the free-streaming, hydrodynamization, and hydrodynamic regimes, with matching conditions ensuring continuity of the rate and of the underlying current–current correlator across regime boundaries; and
(b) extends the computation beyond the conformal boost-invariant 0+1-dimensional approximation to backgrounds with transverse inhomogeneities (and, more generally, non-conformal, non-boost-invariant 3+1-dimensional evolution), producing event-by-event predictions for photon and dilepton spectra integrated over the full spacetime history of the collision.

Provide explicit calculational schemes (within QCD kinetic theory, holographic methods, or hybrid approaches) realizing (a) and (b), and quantify the resulting electromagnetic yields and their dependence on the initial-state transverse profile.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open research direction in relativistic heavy-ion phenomenology. Recent works compute pre-equilibrium photon and dilepton rates in conformal boost-invariant 0+1D kinetic theory and holography, but a fully consistent treatment across free-streaming, hydrodynamization and hydrodynamic stages including transverse inhomogeneities has not been achieved. No published solution claims to resolve the full problem.
